nodes.label: Ember design system
nodes.rationale: Brand metaphor: smith = forge. Background is dark iron, accent is ember; everything active glows and everything historical cools.

nodes.label: Surface elevation tokens
nodes.rationale: The fallback uses the 256-colour cube, not the 16 named ANSI colours, because with those the three surfaces all collapse to Black and DarkGray/Gray collides with text tokens. surface.base is painted, not inherited — inheriting is what made a light theme impossible.

nodes.label: Theme presets (dark / light / high_contrast)
nodes.rationale: light is not an inversion: each role colour is chosen again against a light background. An unknown name, token or invalid hex aborts initialisation with code 2 — a theme that ignores half of what the config asked for is worse than one that refuses to start.

nodes.label: theme.rs::contrast_ratio and the WCAG AA sweep
nodes.rationale: every_preset_meets_wcag_aa sweeps every foreground/surface pair of every preset. When a pair fails, the colour changes — never the threshold.

nodes.label: Glyph tokens and ASCII fallback
nodes.rationale: A glyph missing from the terminal font becomes a blank cell, and a spinner blinking to nothing reads as a hang — so the fallback is per set, not per character. Theme::unicode lives inside Theme because Theme is already the transcript memo key.

nodes.label: ContextGauge component
nodes.rationale: Shows the real numbers because a ratio alone throws away exactly what the user wants to read; an estimated number is drawn with a tilde. Never draw an estimate with the same typography as a measurement. The gauge does not animate.

nodes.label: Per-card focus and per-card throbber
nodes.rationale: Selection and expansion are fields of ChatLine, not App, so they stay out of LayoutKey — a global expansion flag would invalidate the whole transcript on every Enter. Each card derives its spinner phase from its own started_at so two tools spin out of phase.

nodes.label: Overlay reading panel (/usage, /mcp, Ctrl+L)
nodes.rationale: Not a Modal variant: every Modal variant carries a oneshot the agent is blocked on, so a fourth variant would let /usage replace a pending permission request and hang the turn forever.

nodes.label: Sidebar tabs and the 27-column divider
nodes.rationale: A tab trades 'see everything, truncated' for 'see one thing, whole', the right trade in a 28-column panel. Clipping via Tabs does not work — it discards the last title entirely, producing a selectable invisible tab.

nodes.label: The 80x24 layout contract
nodes.rationale: Normative: every new widget has to fit it before being written, because adapting later is what makes acceptance criterion #7 fail late. Nothing shown at any width may make App::is_animating() true.

nodes.label: The context strip
nodes.rationale: Nothing that only exists in the sidebar may be the only place a vital lives — when the sidebar disappears its vitals descend into the strip.

nodes.label: Vertical budget by priority
nodes.rationale: The transcript floor is what the table exists to protect: the old order (input grows to 10 against height-3) left the transcript with 6 lines as soon as the user typed '/'.

nodes.label: Box width invariant (fit_lines)
nodes.rationale: Without it the outer Wrap{trim:false} folds the line and throws the closing border onto the next row — the root cause of the misalignments.

nodes.label: Remappable [keys] (five actions)
nodes.rationale: Ctrl+B is tmux's default prefix and Ctrl+O is discard in a standard termios line discipline — factory settings of the two programs most likely to be around a terminal agent. Enter/Esc/Backspace/arrows and Ctrl+C stay fixed so a config error cannot produce a terminal you can neither type in nor leave.
